_meta.method: Read issue #30 and PR #78 (all comments) and glovebox-options.md on PR #78's head branch (copilot/look-up-glovebox-options). LabX returned an empty HTTP 202 (bot challenge) to the runner, so the listing HTML was fetched read-only through the CubXL Pi (one curl to stdout, --limit-rate 400k, ~225 kB); its 44 photos came straight from cdn.labx.com on the runner (~41 MB, no Pi traffic). The data plate, fascia badge, QA sticker and AtmosPure label were read from those photos. Labconco documents were downloaded from labconco.com's CDN (ctfassets): the current Protector CA manual 5426400 Rev G (2023, Appendix B dimension drawing, rendered at 300-400 dpi and read), the product page, and the Precise CA spec sheet (to rule the 'Precise' label out). The 2001-era manual 50755 Rev E (2002) came from expotechusa.com (PDF) and manualsdir.com. Cole-Parmer's legacy 5060000/5070000 pages are Cloudflare-challenged from both the runner and the Pi and were not read. MSE product data came from the Shopify product .json on the runner. 'estimated_keys' are photo-scaled or inferred; everything else has a source quote. The inches values from Labconco drawings are exact, and mm = in x 25.4 rounded to 0.1 mm.
not_done: No tape-measure check of the actual unit: the seller's 38 in height and 40 in depth disagree with the current-model drawing (45.7 in, 34.4 in), and no 2001-era dimension drawing was found.
The data plate suffix -9147 was not confirmed with Labconco.

choice.why: The lab's latest explicit cheap pick is still the used Labconco controlled-atmosphere glove box with stand, $2,999, private seller in Birmingham, Alabama (PR #78, item #8). Gage Erickson proposed it on 2026-07-20 (https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/pull/78#issuecomment-5025726050: "I'm thinking the $3000 upgradeable option might be our best bet for now.") and Sterling Baird agreed the same day (https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/pull/78#issuecomment-5028159005: "The alabama listing looks nice, and I think with shipping it could be sub-$5k."). Nothing has been bought or quoted since. On 2026-09-17 the interim spec said the box 'likely will be made of plexi glass' (https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/issues/30#issuecomment-5717179521). On 2026-09-23 Gage asked about the MSE acrylic box, and Claude's 2026-09-25 eBay survey suggested a Plas-Labs 830-ABB, a Cleatech or a Terra (https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/issues/30#issuecomment-5828568081). No lab member has picked any of those. So the Labconco is modelled as the primary and the MSE PRO acrylic box with airlock as the alternative.
caveats: The LabX record's own availability window is product_available_from 2024-04-13 to product_available_to 2024-07-12, although is_active=1. The listing may be stale, so confirm it is still for sale.

The earlier comments treated this unit as 'purge-level as sold, AtmosPure-upgradable' and 'fiberglass liner (not groundable)'. The photos and data plate show otherwise: it is a stainless-lined Protector (catalog 50701) that already has a 2001-vintage AtmosPure 51218-00 recirculating purifier. The purifier's condition and regeneration state are unknown, and no O2/H2O monitors are visible.
choice.mse_note_2026-10-03: Modelled on request in PR #240 (2026-10-03). The box exists in two versions and MSE's own documents disagree: the listing shows a vertical-front box with a 400 x 400 mm square side door, while the bundled maker's manual (Changsha MITR, MT008-B) lists a 300 mm round side door and its photos show a sloped front. The model follows the listing photo.

labconco_ca.name: Labconco Protector Controlled Atmosphere Glove Box, single width, Type 304 stainless steel liner, automatic Pressure Control Module, 115 V; fitted with an AtmosPure 51218-00 gas purifier; on a Labconco mobile base stand with casters
labconco_ca.catalog_decoded: In Labconco's 2002 scheme (manual 50755 Rev E), 50600/50700/50800 = basic / + automatic pressure control module / + purge-fill module. The 5th digit is 0 for a fiberglass liner and 1 for stainless. The -00/-02 suffix is 115 V / 230 V. So 50701-00 = stainless liner, automatic pressure control, 115 V. The trailing 9147 is not in the manual. It is probably a factory special, which would fit the purifier being factory-integrated rather than the stock accessory cabinet (unconfirmed). The current catalog scheme (5426400 Rev G) uses 50600/50601 manual and 50800/50801 auto instead.
labconco_ca.series: Protector (fascia badge reads 'LABCONCO PROTECTOR GLOVE BOX'). It is NOT a Precise box, despite the listing text. The Precise CA box has a one-piece polyethylene shell, measures 52.7 x 31.6 x 40.0 in, and has a cylindrical 11.0 in ID x 12.0 in transfer chamber.
labconco_ca.electrical: 115 V, 1 phase, 60 Hz, 20 A (data plate). The 2002 manual asks for a 115 V 60 Hz 20 A receptacle.

_meta.frame: x to the right seen from the glove (front) side, y away from the viewer (front face y=-300, back face y=+300), z up from the bench, origin at the centre of the main box footprint. mm.
_meta.method: Fetched the GB0068899 Shopify JSON (1 image) and its linked manual PDF (SharePoint, MITR-sourced: path '202604_MITR glove box'); pulled every image from MSE's acrylic-glove-box collection JSON (23 listings) and two archived (Wayback) older MSE listings (GB0016/GB0022, a different OEM design); identified the OEM as Changsha MITR Instrument Equipment (model MT008-B) and pulled its Made-in-China MT008 listing, mitrmill.com Type-B page and mictr.com Type-B page (spec tables + photos). Looked at every image. Positions were scaled from the best copy of the listing photo (MITRGlovebox1.jpg, 3000 px but upscaled from ~1000 px) by fitting a pinhole camera to the main box corners using the known 900 x 700 front face and 600 depth (fit: camera ~3.1 m in front of the front face, ~1.06 m above the bench, nearly centred; front face fits 900x700 to <1 %), then back-projecting features onto their wall planes. Typical scaling error ~5-10 % (~±20-30 mm).
not_done: No dimensioned drawing of this box exists in any source found; every position below is scaled from one low-resolution, generic photo (the same image is used on all six MSE 'with airlock' sizes, so it is not proven to be the 900 model, though its 1.275 front aspect ratio matches 900x700 to 1 %).
Glove ports are hidden by the inflated gloves; port centres were taken from the glove bulbs, which sit in front of the panel.
No back, top or right-end view of the rectangular variant was found; the back-wall cable gland, socket strip and main-chamber inlet valve positions are weak.
Labzee (MITR relabel, e.g. BZAGB-509B) returned 403; it was not fetched via the CubXL Pi (judged low value). Alibaba/Amazon/Landt (MA-008) listings were not mined beyond search snippets.

Conflict not resolved: MSE listing says 'Square door 400*400mm' and the photo shows a square latched door, but the bundled MITR manual and MITR tables say 'Left Round Door 300 mm' and MITR's own photos show a sloped-front box. Which variant ships is a question for MSE (sales@msesupplies.com).
Airlock 240 cube: inner vs outer not stated; the photo scales to ~225-235 mm outer.
